headlines.title: What we know about the changes Meta will roll out for teens and parents
headlines.description: Wednesday, Facebook and Instagram’s parent company, Meta, announced it had reached a settlement with the attorneys general from across the country (including California) in the social media addiction lawsuit playing out in an Oakland courtroom. As part of the settlement, Meta agreed to pay out around $18 billion to the states involved and to make changes to its apps. Based on the details of the settlement, the first of those changes are set to roll out in a matter of months, others will take more than a year. The changes for users under 18 include: Two-hour daily limits for use which teens will need parents’ permission to turn off Blocking Meta apps from midnight to 6 a.m. Stronger age verification measures Hiding the number of likes or reactions on posts Blocking teens from using what Meta calls “extreme makeup filters” Muting notifications from 8 a.m. to 3 p.m. for “school mode” Sending prompts to teens after 15 minutes of continuous screentime on Instagram and Facebook Allowing teens to choose a non-algorithmic feed Allowing teens to turn off the autoplay setting Adding new parental controls like telling parents when a teen links a secondary account to their app or interacts with an account that is potentially suspicious Meta also said it’s working to catch and remove underage accounts on their apps and find accounts that may belong to people younger than 13. “The framework we’ve negotiated will empower parents to easily manage how their children access our platforms,” said C.J. Mahoney, Meta’s Chief Legal Officer, in a prepared video statement. The settlement states that within one year, Meta must adopt an “age assurance framework” which must be tested annually by an accredited third party. Within six months, Meta is expected to roll out efforts to detect users under the age of 13. Within four months, Meta is required to implement pauses after they have been using Meta apps continuously for more than 15 minutes and when their total daily usage hits 60 minutes and 90 minutes “to encourage intentional use.” Tech and legal experts say questions remain about how Meta will verify a user’s age without creating new privacy concerns. “The industry was not really very serious about it for a long time, 20 years,” said Ahmed Banafa, Professor of Engineering at San Jose State. Banafa said from a technical standpoint, he expects the age verification measures to be the most difficult parts of the agreement for Meta to fulfill. He explained the debate about how to do this has been “between privacy and protection.” Some legal experts say that is a difficult balance to strike. Nora Benavidez, Senior Counsel at the organization Free Press, has been following this case and noted, “I think one of my other biggest concerns and outstanding questions is about children and their safety and parents’ decisions about how much information they will have to give over to prove the children’s age.” Benavidez wondered how many users across the impacted states will be required to share personal data including age with Meta under these changes. “These are going to be very complicated months ahead,” Benavidez said of the expected rollout of these changes, adding that “parents have a tremendous role right now, in this very uncertain and contentious period.” Alyssa Goard has the full report in the video above.

headlines.title: Deadly crash shuts down northbound Montague Expressway in Santa Clara
headlines.description: A deadly crash has shut down a portion of Montague Expressway Wednesday afternoon in Santa Clara, police said. Northbound Montague Expressway at Mission College Boulevard is closed while police investigate. Motorists should avoid the area and use alternate routes, police said. There is no estimated reopening time and no other information was immediately available. This story uses functionality that may not work in our app. Click here to open the story in your web browser.

headlines.title: East Bay Nepalese community worried after catastrophic floods near Nepal and China border
headlines.description: More than 100 people are dead following the catastrophic flooding near the border of Nepal and China, and a Bay Area man from the impacted area is fearing the worst. The East Bay has a big Nepalese community, especially in Richmond, were a cultural celebration was held with worry looming over it. Videos coming from near the Nepal and China border are unimaginable, and those videos have been watched by most people at the Richmond gathering. “A lot of my friends are not founded yet, so they are missing,” said Janak Raj Dhungana, who is from the devastated area. “I’m sure they are not coming back again.” The country’s police service said at least 157 have been killed, but that number expected to rise in the days to come. Crews now begin the desperate search for survivors and that includes hundreds of tourists and dozens from the U.S. “The problem is this is a very big time for tourist who go to Tibet so right now this is a main route that people travel for Nepal to Tibet,” Former Nepal Trek Guide Lhakpa Gelu Sherpa said. “One of the reasons it’s very popular it’s very close to Kathmandu.” What caused the colossal disaster wasn’t immediately clear, but climate experts in the country say an avalanche from a glacier most likely prompted the flash flood. The USGS also reported a 4.4 magnitude quake in the area. This came at the same time Hindus, who make up the biggest religion in Nepal, celebrate a festival for renewal and spiritual protection. Folks attending Wednesday’s event said this festival is a bittersweet one. “It’s really hard because we can just pray for them. We cannot do anything,” Dhungana said.

headlines.title: San Francisco projects continued tourism growth into 2027
headlines.description: After years of a post-pandemic slump, San Francisco’s travel association says tourism spending is growing and is expected to keep booming into 2027. SF Travel released its latest tourism forecast Wednesday, saying there is still work ahead while simultaneously celebrating improvement and the expectation of a third straight year of growing crowds. “We had a couple of big events, as you know, Super Bowl, FIFA World Cup, things of that nature, but also what really anchored things was the convention calendar,” SF Travel President and CEO Anna Marie Presutti said. “We had more conventions this year than last and we have more conventions next year than this year.” For 2026, hotel occupancy should run about 70% citywide, which is higher than last year. Next year, the expectation is closer to 72%. “Domestic travel seems to be up,” Presutti said. “We’re not seeing a great lift out of international yet, so there are some geopolitical things that are going on there that kind of prevent that, but we are seeing it inch up a little bit.” Next year, 25 million visitors are expected – up from 2026 – and visitor spending is expected to reach over $10 billion.

headlines.title: ICE agent's gun found in SFO bathroom
headlines.description: A flight attendant found an ICE agent’s gun unattended in a public restroom at San Francisco International Airport last month, NBC Bay Area’s Investigative Unit has confirmed. The gun was found in the stall of a men’s bathroom past the security checkpoint in Terminal 2 on the evening of July 21, according to SFO public information officer Doug Yakel. The flight attendant who found it reported the gun to security staff, who closed the restroom to the public and called 911, Yakel said in an email. San Francisco police officers responded within minutes and were on scene when the ICE officer later returned to retrieve the lost firearm, Yakel said. It’s still unclear how long the gun was left sitting in the bathroom before it was found. The airport reported the incident to TSA for potential follow-up action, Yakel added. It’s unclear what the ICE agent was doing at SFO or whether he has faced any discipline. Yakel said the airport wasn’t privy to the nature of ICE’s presence at the airport that evening, and ICE has not responded to questions sent Wednesday morning by NBC Bay Area. Ukrainian immigrant Iryna Gorb was arrested by ICE agents at SFO the following day. Video of her arrest was captured and posted online by Richmond city councilmember Doria Robinson. A Department of Homeland Security spokesperson said Gorb lawfully entered the U.S in 2010 but overstayed her visa by more than 15 years. NBC Bay Area’s Investigative Unit learned of the ICE agent’s lost gun through a public records request seeking further details on Gorb’s arrest. An internal email contained within a batch of records the airport released this week alluded to an “event where an ICE agent left his gun in the MRR near Checkpoint D in TB2.” The airport provided additional details Wednesday afternoon in response to questions from NBC Bay Area. ICE presence at U.S. airports has made headlines across the country in recent weeks, with immigration attorneys reporting an uptick in airport arrests and warning clients about flying. It’s unclear exactly how many immigrants have been arrested at SFO, but Yakel told NBC Bay Area the airport is aware of three such arrests since March, including the arrest of Gorb. Yakel said the airport is “not involved in decisions about DHS or ICE operations” and doesn’t “assist in immigration enforcement, consistent with Sanctuary City policies.” NBC Bay Area obtained CCTV footage of another such arrest on March 22 that also led to widespread public outcry after bystanders filmed the incident and posted it on social media. The third arrest took place on May 1, Yakel said. NBC Bay Area will update the story as we learn more.

headlines.title: Public records request reveals more details about SFO incidents
headlines.description: New details obtained from a public records request related to a high-profile detention of a traveler at San Francisco International Airport reveal a surprising incident that happened one day before. According to SFO, a U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement agent left his gun in a public restroom. Public records obtained from SFO disclose a July 22 incident involving an ICE agent leaving his gun in a public restroom inside Terminal 2. In details provided by an airport spokesperson, a flight attendant entered the men’s restroom post-security and found an unattended gun in one of the stalls. That flight attendant reported it to the security checkpoint staff, who closed the restroom and called 911. The airport spokesperson tells NBC Bay Area the San Francisco police showed up at the restroom in Terminal 2 within 5 minutes, and were there when the ICE agent returns to retrieve the gun. So far, the airport spokesperson has not shared any further information about how long the unsecured gun was in the men’s restroom until police arrived. Airport staff reported the incident to the Transportation Security Administration, which is part of the Department of Homeland Security. NBC Bay Area reached out to the DHS for further comment, but did not receive a response Wednesday. A day after the incident involving the ICE agent’s gun, federal agents detained Iryna Gorb in Terminal 1. Newly released video from SFO shows Gorb exiting her plane at Gate B8 with a man starting to follow her. In another angle, video shows that man pulling her toward him. Gorb in the video tries to pull away, while a second man stays nearby and watches. When the men take Gorb to the ground, bystanders being recording and start asking what is happening as she cries out for help. Some people also called 911 when it was unclear what was going on. According to police dispatch audio, witnesses said they though a passenger might be attacking another passenger. Officers quickly confirmed it was an ICE operation by calling the agency directly. DHS said Gorb was detained because she overstayed her visa. She remains in ICE custody at a detention facility in a California city. Gorb’s friends continue to keep in touch with her and said it is not easy. “It’s constantly difficult to keep in touch,” said Andy Ebiln, Gorb’s friend. “Systems don’t work the way they should. We’ve had scheduled visits that we were told later were not processed correctly.” Gorb’s friends at Hedge Coffee in San Francisco are planning a fundraiser for her next month. According to information from attorneys who track ICE detentions, Gorb is one of three people detained at SFO this year.

headlines.title: Program suspension brings new challenge for UC Berkeley international students
headlines.description: A new order from President Donald Trump, and a warning from Homeland Security, has at least half a dozen UC schools pausing programs that international students need to get working internships – UC Berkeley is one of those schools. Earlier this month, UC schools announced they were temporarily suspending the program. Those suspensions started after a notice from the U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement Office. The agency warned schools that participate in the Student and Exchange Visitor program would face increased risk of investigation by federal agencies. “It would’ve been nice to at have least the ability to take an internship here, so that actually does suck,” UC Berkley International student Leander Hirsch said. CPT allows for F-1 visa students to take part in internships. On Aug. 13, the UC Berkeley International Office issued a lengthy statement outlining the changes. In the statement, the office says they are suspending CPT applications considered “integral to the program of study but are not a degree requirement.” The bottom line, it’s going to be harder for international students to find work in their field of study. “We are in the land of the free and you should be able to work or at least expand your horizon through internships not just college experience,” Hirsch said. UC Berkeley says it made the move to reduce risks to the university and avoid potential immigration issues for students. Some students say they’re still trying to figure out if they’re affected. “If it impacts me directly that would suck, of course, but I will have to check with all the offices,” UC Berkley International student Matteo Martullo said. As for how long the program could stay paused, the International Office also says they are consulting with lawyers to figure out how to proceed.

headlines.title: San Jose officer hospitalized after shootout leaves robbery suspect dead
headlines.description: A San Jose police sergeant who was shot by an armed robbery suspect suffered critical injuries but has since been stabilized, police said Wednesday. The confrontation unfolded Tuesday after officers spotted a suspect wanted in connection with two armed robberies reported over the weekend, according to the San Jose Police Department. When officers approached the suspect, identified by officials as 39-year-old Anthony Chavez of Campbell, police said he pulled out a firearm and sped off, striking multiple vehicles along the way. Chavez later crashed into parked vehicles near Lick Avenue and Goodyear Street and continued fleeing on foot, police said. He eventually reached the area of Almaden Avenue and Floyd Street, where police said he ran to a nearby home occupied by a family and forced his way inside to hide. Officers entered the home, evacuated the family and searched for Chavez, eventually finding him in a small bathroom. As the officers entered the bathroom, Chavez opened fire, striking Sgt. Matt Walsh twice, police said. Walsh and the other officer returned fire, striking Chavez multiple times. Chavez died at the scene. “I’ve watched the body-worn camera of that gunfight in that small bathroom, and what unfolded in that extraordinarily confined space was chilling,” San Jose police Chief Paul Joseph said. “But what was equally striking was Sgt. Walsh’s composure after being shot.” Brett Bymaster, whose children and grandchildren were inside the home, said they hid in a closet before officers arrived and got them out safely. “Officers busted the door down,” Bymaster said, praising their bravery. “They rushed everyone out and we’re incredibly grateful.” Joseph said Chavez had “an extensive violent criminal history.” Chavez was wanted in connection with two armed robberies over the weekend in which he allegedly threatened two people with a weapon described as a long gun. “A criminal history check revealed convictions for a variety of serious and violent crimes, including robbery, assault with a deadly weapon, auto theft, narcotics and much more,” Joseph said. Detectives are continuing to investigate the shooting. The shooting was San Jose police’s second officer-involved shooting of 2026.

headlines.title: Man poses as a 49ers player to defraud women in Oregon, authorities say
headlines.description: A man was accused of pretending to be a San Francisco 49ers player to defraud women in Oregon, according to the United States Attorney’s Office, District of Oregon. According to court documents, beginning in February 2022, Daejon Labrayae Love, 35, and Taylor Jamie Chan, 18, created fictitious investments to defraud numerous women in Oregon, Washington, Idaho and California. Love would meet most of the women through dating apps and pretend to have a lavish lifestyle on social media, falsely portraying himself as a 49ers’ player or a wealthy real estate investor, according to authorities. The Attorney’s Office said Love convinced these victims they were in sincere romantic relationship with him, that he was a sophisticated investor and that Chan was his “investment adviser,” who helped Love to grow a fortune of tens of millions of dollars. Love told the victims he wanted to build wealth and a future with them, authorities said. Officials added Love advertised nonexistent investment vehicles, claiming these investments would generate massive returns for both him and his victims. Court documents said Love used phone apps to create fictitious bank and investment accounts and balances to show the victims and legitimize the scheme. Authorities said Love and Chan exchanged electronic communications in which Chan pretended to be Love’s investment adviser and would send messages encouraging Love to invest in new opportunities. Love would then send screenshots of those messages to the victims to convince them to send money to either of them, according to court documents. The Attorney’s Office said the pair would have video calls with the victims to show them falsified investment gains and encourage them to part with their money. Authorities added if the victims did not have money, Love sometimes instructed them to take a loan; if they were left with no more money to invest, or asked too many questions, Love would block them, stop any communication with them and keep the money. Financial records show the pair received about $1.3 million from victim investors, according to authorities. Officials said 26 victims have been identified, but the FBI believes there could be more. Authorities said they both were arrested when Chan flew from California on Aug. 24 to meet Love in Boise, Idaho. Both were charged with conspiracy to commit wire fraud and wire fraud. The FBI encourages anyone with information on Love and/or Chan to submit a tip at the FBI website https://tips.fbi.gov/home or to call 1-800-CALL-FBI.

headlines.title: San Jose police arrest alleged strong-armed jewelry thieves
headlines.description: Police in San Jose arrested an alleged ring of jewelry thieves who forcibly robbed elderly people, the department said Tuesday. Last Thursday just before 3 p.m., officers in San Jose responded to a strong-armed robbery in a parking lot in the 5300 block of Almaden Expressway. According to the victim, who is an elderly woman, a woman approached her and forcibly took her ring and gold chain necklace before taking off in a car being driven by a man. Investigators were able to identify the car used in the robbery and on Friday, the car was located in Concord, where someone else reported a strong-armed robbery outside of a business. The suspects’ vehicle was then tracked through license plate cameras back to San Jose at a business located in the 2200 block of Senter Road. Officers made contact with the suspects and two men and one woman were detained: Ruxandra Constantin, 30, Caldararu Constantin, 36, and Constantin Constantin, 34. While the trio was being arrested, another elderly woman approached police and said she had just been robbed of her gold chain necklace, allegedly by the suspects. Police said they located a bag with gold and jewelry in it in the possession of Ruxandra Constantin. Investigators believe the three are responsible for an additional grand theft of a gold chain necklace on Aug. 16 in a parking lot in the 5300 block of Almaden Expressway, where an elderly man was robbed. According to police, chain snatch robberies have been an increasing trend not only in the city of San Jose but throughout the Bay Area. “In these cases, the suspects typically approach elderly victims walking in public and forcibly remove the gold chain necklace off the person,” the San Jose Police Department said. “Often times, the suspects will use distraction techniques, such as selling jewelry, striking up a conversation, or swapping the jewelry out without the victim’s knowledge.” Due to the nature of these crimes, detectives believe there may be additional victims. Anyone with information about these cases or similar cases is asked to contact Detective Thandi at 4415@sanjoseca.gov or 408-277-4166.

headlines.title: Napa Valley wineries serve up new ‘experiences' amid sobering economic downturn
headlines.description: Tourism to Napa Valley historically brings in more than $2 billion each year, but fewer visitors and higher costs have winemakers across the region worried about an increasingly difficult financial landscape. “It’s not just the big guys that are getting hurt, it’s not just the little guys that getting hurt, it’s everybody in between,” said Christi Ficeli, owner of Goosecross Cellars in Napa Valley. “This economy is hard for everybody, even the people that own wineries in Napa.” This economy is hard for everybody, even the people that own wineries in Napa Christi Ficeli, owner of Goosecross Cellars in Napa Valley Ficeli, who runs the family-owned winery with her husband, Dave Ficeli, says visitation at the winery is down 40% from five years ago. “Cash is tight right now – the economy is tough on us,” she said. “Prices are increasing.” While Napa’s famed vintages are made locally, supplies often come from abroad and tariffs have resulted in higher prices. Wine barrels from France, glass bottles from China, and corks from Portugal have all increased in price, according to Ficeli, and rising gas prices have made those supplies even more expensive to transport. “Our costs have gone up 10% to 12% and our pricing has gone up 1% to 2%,” Ficeli said. “We’re absorbing a lot of that here.” Christi Ficeli has run Goosecross Cellars in Napa Valley for the past 13 years with her husband Dave Ficeli. To offset higher costs, Ficeli’s winery is now focusing on more than just wine. To attract new customers and keep guests coming back, Goosecross has been hosting an array of events at its vineyard, including movie nights and comedy shows. “We’ve started doing more events because I think people want experience – they want things that are different,” she said. “We’re trying to bring some new and exciting things to the visitors that are here in Napa.” Ficeli is also investing in customer retention by recently expanding her staff from 12 to 13 employees, with the newest hire dedicated to keeping existing customers. Ellie Leigh was recently hired for the newly created customer-retention position. “Personal touch points, handwritten invitations, and notes has been really top of mind,” Leigh told Ficeli during a recent meeting at the winery. Ellie Leigh is the newest hire at Goosecross Cellars, where she is responsible for retaining customers and boosting wine subscriptions as the winery’s head of estate partnerships. I know it’s going to hurt to add another staff member, but if she can save a customer from leaving our program and keep them around for a little bit longer, it’s going to be worth every penny I’m spending on her. Winery owner Christi Ficeli explains why she hired a new employee to focus on customer retention “I know it’s going to hurt to add another staff member, but if she can save a customer from leaving our program and keep them around for a little bit longer, it’s going to be worth every penny I’m spending on her,” Ficeli told the Investigative Unit. “It’s so much more expensive to gain a new customer than to keep one.” For winery owners across Napa Valley, simply resting on the region’s laurels as a top-tier destination may no longer be enough to keep customers coming through the door. “It definitely has changed,” Ficeli said. “Mostly because there’s less people coming to Napa.” The region welcomed 3.8 million visitors last year, about 50,000 fewer than visited in 2018, according to Visit Napa Valley, Napa County’s tourism marketing organization. While Napa visitation has rebounded in recent years, it remains below its pre-pandemic peak. At the same time, fewer Americans are drinking wine. Only about 29% of adults in America drink wine compared to 34% three years ago, according to the Wine Market Council, a research firm that tracks consumer wine spending. Napa Valley tourism rates near pre-pandemic levels Adding to the challenge is the cost of traveling to wine country. The average hotel room in Napa Valley now costs about $420 a night – a 25% increase since before the pandemic, according to Visit Napa Valley. “We’ve done some estimates, it’s probably about $5,000 just to stay here for the weekend before you even walk through the door of a winery,” Ficeli said. “Hotel, flight, rental car, and food … all up.” Tasting prices have also climbed. The average tasting fee in Napa is now about $80, according to a recent wine industry report by Silicon Valley Bank. Food & Drink Jun 10 Napa County Apr 22, 2025 “We’re going through a really tough time,” said Tom Davies, who runs V. Sattui, a 50-year-old winery with more than 100 employees. “What’s at stake here is the sustainability of our wine industry.” Davies said the economy forced him to change pricing, too, but not in the way you might think. Two days a week, he dropped his tasting fee to zero to attract new business. We have to open our doors wider. Tom Davies, President and Managing Partner of V. Sattui Winery Tom Davies is president and managing partner of V. Sattui Winery in Napa Valley. “We have to open our doors wider,” Davies said. “I want to even be more accessible than we’ve ever been before.” Davies said the move to offer three complimentary pours has boosted wine sales. So much so, he’s now offering the free tasting menu three days a week. “We’re selling more wine than we were when we were charging every day,” he said. Davies remembers when all tastings in Napa were free. He said his idea to bring free tastings back is a nod to the past and an investment in the future – not only for his winery but for the entire Napa Valley. “The real payoff would be down the road when we can get the kind of visitation back to the vineyards that we had back 10 years ago,” he said. “I just want to make sure we can continue on.” Whether it’s larger wineries like his or smaller ones like Christi Ficeli’s down the road, the financial strain has been hard to swallow. I would say 2026 is one of the hardest years we’ve had so far outside of Covid. Christi Ficeli has run Goosecross Cellars for the past 13 years with her husband Winery owner Christi Ficeli takes Senior Investigative Reporter Bigad Shaban on a tour of her Napa Valley vineyard at Goosecross Cellars. “I would say 2026 is one of the hardest years we’ve had so far outside of Covid,” she said. “We’re working to cut costs everywhere we can.” Despite the financial squeeze, Ficeli remains hopeful. Like so many winery owners in Napa Valley, she’s holding on to a glass-half-full kind of optimism. “I love what I do,” she said. “When people come to Napa, they’re celebrating – 99.9% of the people who walk through our door are already happy and I get to make them that much happier by giving them an experience.” Contact The Investigative Unit submit tips | 1-888-996-TIPS | e-mail Bigad Follow @BigadShaban on social media Bigad Shaban This story uses functionality that may not work in our app. Click here to open the story in your web browser.

headlines.title: VTA Orange Line fully reopens after electrical issue
headlines.description: VTA’s Orange Line returned to full service Wednesday morning after an electrical issue disrupted service at four stations for about a day, transit officials said. VTA crews worked overnight to make repairs after an electrical line issue cut power to four Orange Line stations at about 6 a.m. Tuesday. Full service resumed at all Orange Line stations at 7 a.m. Wednesday, according to VTA. The agency did not immediately provide additional details about what caused the electrical issue.
